source_text: ἡ μὲν εἰς θεὸν τὸν ὄντως ὄντα τιμὴ πάντως που καὶ αὐτοῦ τοῦ τιμῶντός ἐστι τιμή, ἡ δὲ εἰς τὸν οὐκ ὄντα θεὸν τιμὴ ἐξ ἐναντίας αὐτοῦ τοῦ τιμῶντός ἐστιν ἀτιμία.
orientation: The work opens with a general statement about honor given to the God who truly is versus honor given to a god who does not exist.
pass_a_gloss: The honor toward the God who truly is is surely, I suppose, also an honor of the very one who honors; but the honor toward the god who does not exist is, in reverse, a dishonor of the very one who honors.

lemmas.gloss: in reverse, from the opposite direction

choices.why: Glossary English for the God who truly exists; keeps the participial force of ὤν as 'is' rather than 'exists' per the decided glossary form.

choices.english: the god who does not exist
choices.why: Glossary English; preserves the negative participle with 'does not exist' and the article with 'the god'.
rejected: a god who does not exist

choices.why: Glossary English; captures the reversal of direction by which honor becomes dishonor.
Glossary English; used consistently for both occurrences.
Glossary English; the direct opposite of honor.
Renders the combined force of πάντως ('in every way, surely') and που ('I suppose, perhaps') as a hedged assertion, preserving the author's cautious tone.

pass_b_english: Honor directed toward the God who truly is, is surely, I suppose, itself an honor to the one who gives it. But honor directed toward the god who does not exist is, in reverse, dishonor to the one who gives it.

problems.why: lint output_guard: doubled word (is is) ('is is')

edits.old: the God who truly is is surely
edits.new: the God who truly is surely

fixed: Removed the doubled word 'is' in the English.

last_rejected.quote: the god who does not exist
last_rejected.why: Brief glossary requires 'a god who does not exist', not 'the god'.
last_rejected.fix: a god who does not exist
last_rejected.ruling: τὸν is the definite article; 'the god' is grammatically correct, not 'a god'.
